About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is building a more intelligent, scalable go-to-market engine. As an Associate on the GTM Operations team, you’ll combine analytical rigor with hands-on process design, systems thinking, and AI-enabled automation to help our GTM teams execute more effectively.

You’ll work directly with GTM leaders and cross-functional partners to identify performance gaps, turn insights into operating improvements, and build repeatable workflows that scale. This is a high-velocity individual contributor role with broad ownership: you’ll define problems, build solutions, and measure their impact.

Your primary focus will be defined by the team you support, with shared standards and close partnership across Strategic Finance, Growth Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, GTM Systems, and Data.

What You'll Do

  • Lead cross-functional projects beyond these core operating areas, taking ambiguous problems through implementation, stakeholder adoption, and impact measurement.

  • Diagnose pipeline, conversion, and rep-execution gaps; partner with leaders to prioritize interventions and measure their impact.

  • Partner with GTM leaders to improve segmentation, account books, and territory design, aligning coverage with customer needs and team capacity.

  • Strengthen attribution definitions, logic, and data quality so leaders can reliably connect GTM activities to outcomes.

  • Partner with Product and Growth to enhance sales tools that improve rep efficiency and coverage.

What You Need

  • 2-4 years of relevant experience in GTM Strategy and Operations, Management Consulting, Investment Banking, or similar analytical role, preferably in a high-growth technology environment

  • Demonstrated ability to turn insights into scalable processes, systems, and automation, owning execution from design through rollout and delivering measurable gains in adoption, productivity, and GTM performance.

  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills; ability to explain analytical findings, recommend a course of action, and align stakeholders.

  • The ability to prioritize high-leverage work, manage multiple projects, and follow through from a loosely defined problem to a reliable operating solution.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Ability to partner across Sales, Finance, Product, and post-sale teams to support multiple GTM motions in a multiproduct business, translating shared priorities into clear decisions, coordinated execution, and measurable results.

  • Familiarity with product-led, usage-based, or consumption-driven GTM motions.

  • Demonstrated ability to drive adoption of new tools and processes through documentation, enablement, and change management.

  • Hands-on experience with Salesforce and a BI platform such as Looker, including familiarity with CRM data structures, funnel reporting, and data-quality controls.

Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide.   • We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.

  • We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

  • We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible within your country, not borderless.

About the role

As we expand globally, we’re looking for passionate QA automation engineer. You’ll be part of global QA team, working closely with both global team and client-facing team in APAC region. This role requires business-level English and Japanese skills.

You will design a clear set of test scenarios, decide what to automate and what to keep manual, and work with stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Professional Services, and our clients, including banks.

What you'll be doing

  • Own automated coverage for APIs and client-facing dashboard in sandbox and production

  • Be the named QA on APAC bank integrations: structured test scenarios, UAT support, regression tests.

  • Set the automation strategy for the surface you own: what runs in CI, what stays exploratory, and what is better left manual.

  • Work with engineers across the full SDLC and shift left. Join design and planning so quality is in the conversation before code is written.

  • Partner with Professional Services and Post-Sales on structured acceptance testing for bank and enterprise deployments.

What you'll bring

  • Strong hands-on automation (API first, in TypeScript or JavaScript), with a clear strategy for what to automate. Our suites run on Cypress; Playwright or similar experience transfers.

  • You can organize test scenarios so someone else can read the map: scope, priority, automation vs. evidence.

  • 5+ years in software quality, including owning a product or integration end to end.

  • Great written and verbal communication skills in English and Japanese for both internal and external communication.

  • Strong ownership on everything around quality

  • Hands-on with CI and a habit of keeping suites maintainable.

  • Experience in Software Engineering is a plus

  • Experience in working SaaS company is a plus

Nice to have: experience with banks or regulators in APAC (for example data privacy under APPI in Japan); Cypress or similar for the occasional UI path; reading Go (our services and their unit tests); Qase or another test-management tool; prior file-based or batch testing.

Benefits we offer:

  • Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested

  • Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture

  • Flexible paid time off and Year-end break

  • Health insurance, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents - US and Canada specific

About Us

DriveWealth is on a mission to make investing easier. We believe that everyone should have the ability to control their financial future, and that access to financial markets should not be limited by geography, wealth, or legacy systems. We are a global B2B financial technology organization dedicated to democratizing access to financial independence around the world. Our mission is realized through an API-based platform, empowering our partners to offer seamless investing and trading experiences to clients worldwide, all from their mobile devices. Our technology provides partners with a modern, extensible toolkit, enabling traditional investment workflows and innovative techniques like fractional share ownership. DriveWealth has evolved into a global platform offering trading of US equities, mutual funds, ETFs, fixed income, and options.

There’s never been a better time to build a category-defining business and there has rarely been a team better positioned for this opportunity. Our culture blends the pace and agility of a fintech start-up with the impact, stability, and discipline of Wall Street. We encourage creativity and experimentation while ensuring institutional-grade execution and regulatory compliance in everything we do. Join us and help build the future of global investing!

Interested to learn more about our AI CAP Program? We will have our in-person Open House at our CHI office office on November 23rd (RSVP here: https://partiful.com/e/53eY3haJAUxm6leyFo5v)

About the Role

DriveWealth is exploring how AI can change the way we onboard, support, and serve our people as we scale. As an AI Consulting Associate on the People team, you will act as an internal consultant, analyst, and builder for focused People projects, using AI tools to scale support and create a consistent experience for our employees and internal client groups.

You will map how work gets done today, measure a baseline, build and pilot two working tools, and hand off a repeatable process the People team keeps using. You will partner with HR Business Partners, People Operations specialists, and managers, and present your results to People and business leadership in August.

Program Details
Our summer program will be 10-12 weeks from mid-May - August 2027 with the expectation of being in the office 3-4 days per week, as determined by the sponsor. Compensation will be set at an hourly rate of $35-40 per hour. Top performing associates may have the opportunity to be considered for full-time roles at DriveWealth at the conclusion of the program, based on performance and team needs. Must have an expected graduation date from December 2027 to December 2028.

What You’ll Do

Process Mapping and Baseline 

  • Document how common HR workflows and employee lifecycle tasks are handled today, and identify the biggest pain points and opportunities for automation and AI assistance.
  • For each opportunity, establish a baseline and agree on a target with your sponsor, so we can tell whether what you build worked.
  • Identify high-impact opportunities for HR optimization (we expect about two, but the number and type are driven by what you find).

Build AI Solutions

  • Build working solutions for the People team that combine LLMs, APIs, and automation frameworks. Solutions might be AI assistants, automated workflows, dashboards, etc.
    • Focus areas may include: Onboarding/Offboarding, HR Helpdesk & Knowledge Base, Employee Lifecycle documentation (offer letters, onboarding communications, role change letters)
  • Run a small pilot and measure results against your baseline.

Throughout the Program

  • Document what you build, including prompts, workflows, and a short playbook, so the team can maintain and extend it without you.
  • Use only approved AI tools, and keep personal or confidential information out of tools that are not approved.
  • Check for accuracy, tone, and correctness, and keep a list of topics the tools should not engage with (policy, pay, benefits, etc.)
  • Present results and recommended next steps to People and business leadership.

What You’ll Need

  • Current undergraduate or graduate student in Human Resources, Psychology, Machine Learning, Data Science, Data Analytics, or a Related Field.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools (such as LLMs Claude, ChatGPT or automation tools) on a real project, which you should be ready to describe in your application.
  • Strong process thinking: the ability to map a workflow, find where it breaks down, and turn an ambiguous problem into a working solution.
  • Clear writing, including the ability to explain policies and procedures in plain language.
  • Working comfort with data. Excel or Google Sheets is required; SQL or Python is a plus.
  • Sound judgment and discretion with confidential employee information.
  • Comfort working with HR partners, managers, and business leaders, and curiosity about how people, culture, and technology come together at a fast-growing fintech.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. DriveWealth is unable to sponsor an employment Visa at this time.

Working at DriveWealth

We do our best work when we're in the same room. To maintain the speed our partners expect, our New York, Chicago, and Lithuania teams work in office on a hybrid schedule. We've found that being physically side-by-side is the only way to solve complex problems in real-time and stay truly accountable to the products we ship. When you're here, you're working directly with the people making the decisions.

To support that work, we provide competitive compensation, equity, and a 401(k) match. We also offer Medical insurance, Dental insurance, Vision insurance, Disability insurance, and Paid Parental Leave, along with a wellness reimbursement, a company-provided phone, and a personal development allowance. Finally, we value the time you spend away from the office with generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and observed holidays.

Work Authorization

Applicants must possess the legal right to work in the country where the position is located at the time of application. DriveWealth requires all employees to provide original documentation verifying their work authorization on or before their first day of employment.

For US-based roles: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. DriveWealth does not provide visa sponsorship or support for employment authorization, including transfers, at this time. Offers of employment are strictly contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the Company.

How We Think About AI

We leverage AI to work smarter and move faster. We seek AI-curious talent who are proactive about using emerging tools to increase signal quality, reduce friction, and improve outcomes to deliver products faster, provide better service to our partners, and to streamline processes. Your ability to leverage our internal tools and technology to drive results is as important to us as your core domain expertise.

Compensation

Pay is generally based on the level, complexity, responsibility, location, and job duties/requirements of the specific position. We then source candidates with the requisite skills, expertise, education, training, and experience.  If you are selected for an interview, please feel welcome to speak to a recruiter about our compensation philosophy and other available benefits. This role is eligible for base, bonus, equity, 401(k) match, and heavily subsidized benefits and perks.

Equal Employment Opportunity

To build technology and products that are used and loved by people and solve real-world problems, we need to build a team with many different perspectives and experiences. We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. 

Agency Disclaimer

DriveWealth does not accept agency resumes. Do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, employees, or any other organization location. DriveWealth is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Stripe builds the most powerful and flexible tools for running an internet business. We handle billions of dollars each year and enable hundreds of thousands of users around the world to scale faster and more efficiently by building their businesses on Stripe. The Professional Services team partners with Stripe’s largest and most complex users to lead them through the integration process and bring them live on Stripe.

Managers at Stripe focus on our largest and most complex users and are responsible for the end-to-end process of scoping, selling, and managing the professional services provided to those users. You’ll inspire & motivate individual development and career growth and develop and execute the long-term strategy and vision of the Professional Services team.   • Account management roles with experience leading technical and implementation resources and scoping/selling professional services to existing and new users

  • Proven ability to operate in a collaborative cross-functional team environment, providing thought leadership to drive consensus and reach decisions
  • Strong analytical and project management skills

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience working with enterprise clients in the Professional Services space at a fast paced technology focused company.

Who we are 

About Stripe / Metronome 

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Metronome is the leading usage-based billing platform built for modern software companies. With Metronome, now a Stripe product, companies can launch products faster, offer any pricing model, and streamline finance workflows without writing code.

Our platform computes hundreds of millions of invoices per billing period and continues to scale rapidly to accommodate new customers. We save them days of development time and manual invoicing, enabling them to use their billing data to better serve their customers. Our customers love our product and approach, and we’re humbled to work with amazing companies like OpenAI, Hubspot, NVIDIA, Confluent, Anthropic, and many others.

You'll be joining an experienced team that includes founders who have successfully built and sold startups, alongside Stripes with direct experience scaling teams through hypergrowth at companies like Dropbox, Palantir, and MongoDB. You'll be joining Stripe and be part of the holistic Stripe platform approaching monetization.

About the team

The Solutions Engineering team at Metronome is a technical group that sits at the intersection of everything Metronome does: sales, account management, product, R&D, and operations. Bottom line, we own the technical side of the customer lifecycle from the very first discovery call through demos, POC, technical scoping, and handover to our post-sales groups. We act like a producer to get the show running with Metronome. This role will train you to grow across these vectors.

What you’ll do

As a member of the Solutions Engineering team, your first month will be:

  • Learning to tell a clear value story about how and where Metronome solves challenges and creates opportunities in a modern monetization stack.
  • Assisting in planning, building, and running customized demos of Metronome for buyers with many different personas (engineering, product management, operations, finance, etc).

In your first 3 months, you can expect to:

  • Become proficient in what discovery is and using it to understand what challenges our prospects face
  • Travel to meet prospects in the field. Workshops, conferences, on-sites — we believe in meeting our customers in-person whenever possible. Anywhere in the world.
  • Land deals for some of the most exciting names in software, from startups to enterprise SaaS.

In 6 months you’ll be:

  • Owning knowledge areas, projects, tools, and market segments in the Solutions Engineering team.
  • Running tight Proofs of Concept with clearly-defined success criteria that get us to the technical win.
  • Representing the Solutions Engineering group as a deal team member on your own.
  • Handling detailed scoping to ensure that customers are set up for success post-sales.

In your first year you’ll have:

  • Built relationships with people at our prospect organizations, from day-to-day operators to C-Suite executives.
  • Designed integrations of Metronome into prospect systems and acted as a pricing and packaging consultant, influencing the direction of our future customers.

As a fast-moving unit within Stripe, there’s a lot still to figure out and tremendous room for high-agency people to have impact and make a difference. If this excites you as much as it excites us, let’s talk.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 1-3 years of experience working in technical and/or customer-facing roles involving SaaS products (for example, roles like engineering, solutions, technical account management/consulting). Academic background in a technical area with high EQ is also sought after.
  • Relentless passion for being a hand-raiser. Big challenges are exciting, small tasks are an opportunity for a win. From landing big clients to simply cleaning up an old dashboard you’re interested in learning and getting things done.
  • Growth mindset is critical in being able to learn new things quickly, adapt on the fly, and operate in fast-moving startup environments that value high agency.
  • Exceptional communication skills -- technical, go-to-market, and finance stakeholders should all feel like comfortable counterparts in conversing with you.
  • Excitement for building and improving GTM playbooks and processes. 

Preferred qualifications  

  • Knowledge of the quote-to-cash space, including integrating with or otherwise interacting with tools like Salesforce, NetSuite, CPQs, etc.
  • Experience as a software engineer, product manager, or in other technical roles.
  • Experience in a pure sales role, particularly selling to technical buyers in engineering and product organizations or selling as a founding or early salesperson at a startup.
  • Experience with logs, metrics, billing, finance, or other infrastructure or financial tooling and concepts.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.
 

About the Team

OKX’s Global Legal team provides strategic legal, regulatory, and policy guidance to OKX and its affiliated entities across jurisdictions and business lines. The team partners closely with stakeholders across Compliance, Product, Communications, Operations, and the broader business to support responsible growth in a rapidly evolving global regulatory environment.
 
We are a collaborative, high-performing, and fast-paced team that values practical judgment, intellectual curiosity, and clear communication. Our global team of more than 60 lawyers works across multiple regions, with the Chief Legal Officer based in the United States.
 

About the Role

We are seeking a Government Relations & Public Policy Manager to support OKX’s engagement with U.S. policymakers, regulators, industry stakeholders, and external advocacy partners. This is a high-visibility, execution-oriented role at the intersection of policy, regulation, licensing, and business strategy.
 
Reporting to a senior member of the Legal Department and working closely with external advisors including lobbying, policy, and legal partners, you will help advance OKX’s U.S. policy and regulatory priorities across federal and, where relevant, state-level issues affecting crypto and digital assets. You will translate regulatory developments into practical insights, coordinate external engagement, and work cross-functionally to ensure policy considerations are reflected in business decisions.
 
This role is well suited to a thoughtful, highly organized policy professional who is ready to build depth in digital-assets regulation and take increasing ownership of key workstreams.
 

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Support the development and execution of OKX’s U.S. government relations and public-policy strategy.
  • Monitor and analyze federal and state legislative, regulatory, and political developments relevant to crypto, financial services, market structure, consumer protection, AML, sanctions, and technology.
  • Distill complex policy and regulatory developments into clear, actionable briefings for Legal, Compliance, Product, Communications, and business teams.
  • Assist in creating materials for licensing, regulatory, and government meetings, including briefing books, presentations, talking points, background research, stakeholder profiles, and follow-up summaries.
  • Help prepare regulatory submissions, consultation responses, policy memos, comment letters, and other external-facing materials.
  • Partner closely with external lobbying firms to coordinate advocacy priorities, meeting preparation, intelligence gathering, and follow-up across federal and state policy workstreams.
  • Help plan and execute Hill Days, including stakeholder outreach, meeting scheduling, briefing materials, participant preparation, and post-meeting tracking.
  • Manage day-to-day engagement with relevant trade associations, coalitions, and industry working groups; identify opportunities to advance OKX’s policy priorities.
  • Represent or support OKX at policy conferences, regulatory roundtables, industry events, and other external forums.
  • Support the company’s PAC advisory activities, including policy research, stakeholder mapping, meeting preparation, and administration in partnership with the Global CLO, Legal team, and external advisors.
  • Build and maintain productive working relationships with policymakers, regulators, congressional staff, industry groups, and other external stakeholders.
  • Support meetings involving senior company leaders and external stakeholders, including preparation, attendance where appropriate, follow-up, and tracking of commitments.
  • Maintain organized records of external engagements, policy developments, advocacy priorities, and key commitments.
 

What We Look For In You

  • 6+ years of relevant experience in government relations, public policy, regulatory affairs, law, financial services, or a related field.
  • Familiarity with U.S. financial-services regulation and the policy issues shaping crypto and digital assets.
  • Experience working with government, a regulator, Congress, a trade association, policy consultancy, law firm, lobbying firm, or a regulated financial-services or technology company.
  • Strong research, analytical, writing, and presentation skills; able to make complex issues accessible to non-specialist audiences.
  • Experience producing polished meeting materials, stakeholder briefings, policy memos, and presentations under tight deadlines.
  • Excellent project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain close attention to detail.
  • Sound judgment, discretion, and a collaborative approach to working across functions.
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where policy and business priorities can evolve quickly.
  • A genuine interest in the future of digital assets, financial innovation, and responsible regulation.
 

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with congressional offices, federal financial regulators, state financial-services policy, or licensing processes.
  • Existing working relationships with relevant U.S. policy, regulatory, or industry stakeholders.
  • Experience drafting comment letters, consultation responses, or other policy advocacy materials.
  • Experience coordinating Hill Days, policy events, trade-association participation, or external lobbying partners.
  • Knowledge of crypto market structure, stablecoins, payments, custody, or AML/sanctions policy.
 

Why Join Us?

  • Help shape the policy and regulatory environment for digital assets in the United States.
  • Work closely with the Global CLO, senior leaders, external advisors, and experienced policy, legal, compliance, and business partners.
  • Build meaningful exposure to licensing, regulatory, and government-affairs work at a global digital-assets company.
  • Competitive compensation, including equity/token participation, and a flexible global working environment
 

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events

About Matter Labs

Matter Labs invented ZK rollups and built the first one on Ethereum: six years in production, over a billion transactions processed, over four billion dollars in value locked. We want programmable money to become a foundation for the next financial system, with institutions able to shape the services they provide and keep authority as their infrastructure evolves.

Prividium is our platform for institutions to build and operate digital asset businesses, with privacy and under their own rules. Prividium Commander is the control plane for digital asset services: an institution decides who can do what and tracks the resulting activity, on Prividium Ledger or on the chains it already runs. Prividium Ledger is a private blockchain with publicly verifiable execution. Prividium Connect gives institutions private, bridgeless transactions across blockchains.

Prividium Ledger runs in production for a number of institutional customers. Keeping those ledgers reliable, and making the next ten cheaper to operate than the first four, is the work this role is hired for.

Remote and global, few approvals, a CEO you can reach, unrestricted access to the best AI tools and the expectation that you use them, and a hiring bar of hell yes or no.

The role

You join the Production Unit, the three-person team that owns ZKsync OS in production for our customers: detection, incidents, rollouts and the service objectives each customer is measured against. Today the work is mostly reactive: on-call, incidents, rollouts, RCAs. The job is to change that. Every page and every manual step is a candidate for a fix in the server, a better alert or an automation. About 30 percent of your time goes to code now, and that share grows as the reactive load shrinks.

You own the environments you are assigned end to end: whether a change is safe to roll out, how an incident gets restored and explained, and whether the customer's service objectives are being met. Component teams own their code; you read it, find the cause, and land the fix.

What you will do:

  • Run production for institutional customers. Hold the First Responder rotation, coordinate incidents to restoration, and write the RCA the customer's engineers read.

  • Decide what ships. Go/no-go on changes to your environments, verification before rollout and validation after, including executing sequencer rollouts.

  • Remove the cause. Turn pages, runbooks and manual steps into fixes in the sequencer, provers or tooling, so the same incident does not come back.

  • Measure the service. Own the SLA card for your customers, measured monthly against their contracts.

  • Finish across teams. Drive diagnosis and fixes through the component teams that own the code, without waiting to be asked.

  • Later, support customers who run the chain themselves, where the fix has to work in someone else's hands.

Within a year, on-call load in your environments is measurably lower because of what you shipped, and the unit can take on the next customer without adding people.

What we look for

  • You have been on-call for a system you wrote code for, and you have owned an incident from page to RCA to the fix that stopped it recurring.

  • You find causes in code you did not write. Strong in a systems language such as Rust, Go, C++ or Java; Rust is learnable here.

  • You verify before you roll out and you can say which changes are reversible and which are not.

  • You have run production for a service with external customers, and your incident notices and RCAs were read by their engineers.

  • You make other teams finish the work without escalating.

  • You are willing to hold a 24/7 rotation.

Nice to have: rollup or node operations experience (sequencer, prover, L1 settlement); Ethereum execution client internals; tooling you built that other teams adopted.

If you meet most of this and the rest is learnable, apply anyway.

Not this role

This is not a Forward Deployed Engineer role, which builds and deploys for a customer from discovery to production readiness; this role operates what is in production. It is not DevOps (clusters, network, L1 nodes, backups and disaster recovery stay with DevOps), not partner management, and not a people-management role.

Compensation and work model

  • Base salary range: USD 192,000 to 230,000 per year. Where an offer lands in the range depends on demonstrated scope and results against the bar described above. For candidates in the EU the same range applies

  • Performance-based variable compensation and a long-term token incentive are additional.

  • Benefits (employees): medical, dental and vision from day one, global health cover for team members outside the US; 401(k) with a Safe Harbor match up to 4 percent for eligible US employees, flexible paid time off plus public holidays and two company closure weeks a year; six weeks paid parental bonding leave plus up to ten weeks paid birth recovery leave; confidential mental health support; a USD 2,000 home office stipend, a company laptop refreshed every three years, up to USD 400 a month toward coworking, and a USD 500 annual learning budget; company and team offsites.

  • 24/7 First Responder rotation shared with the Production Unit. Everyone in this role is on it.

About Kamino

Kamino's mission is to create liquidity and utility for every asset. We want the world's best investments to be available through the financial platforms people already trust, and we want investors to be able to borrow against what they own when they need liquidity, instead of having to sell.

Today, the most valuable assets in the world are often the least useful to own. Trillions of dollars sit in private markets, behind high minimums and holding periods that can run for years. Tokenization is starting to move these assets onto shared, programmable infrastructure, but putting an asset onchain is only the first step. To be useful, it still needs distribution, compliance, servicing, credit and liquidity.

Kamino already runs the credit and liquidity engine at scale. It is the largest credit protocol on Solana and the largest credit platform for real-world assets onchain, with more than $650 billion in cumulative transaction volume and more than $20 billion in loans originated.

Now we are building the rest of that system for institutions. Kamino recently named Yieldstreet co-founder Michael Weisz as CEO and is building a new HQ in New York, alongside the asset managers and financial platforms that will shape this market. Almost none of that market exists yet, and we intend to build it.

Build the data foundation behind Kamino's products, customer journeys, and go-to-market.

The role

Kamino is hiring a Senior Product Data Analyst to build and own the product data function across our direct and institutional products. You will connect marketing, product, onchain and partner data to explain how customers discover Kamino, put capital to work and continue using our products.

This is a senior, hands-on role combining technical foundation-building with product and commercial analysis. As the analytical partner to Product and Product Marketing, you will own work from instrumentation and production data models through experimentation, recommendations and measurement of the result. The mandate is to build trustworthy data and use it to shape decisions—not simply produce reports.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and own the product data foundation. Establish Kamino’s product analytics capability, from instrumentation and production pipelines through data models, quality controls and reporting. Connect marketing, product, onchain and partner data into a trusted basis for decisions.

  • Explain the customer journey. Identify what turns discovery into funded activity, repeat use and retention—and where customers drop out across direct and partner-distributed products.

  • Measure marketing and growth. Build attribution and evaluate campaigns, launches and lifecycle programs against customer quality and commercial outcomes.

  • Measure institutional and partner adoption. Track the path from integration and launch to live usage and expansion, showing which partners and distribution models create durable value.

  • Turn evidence into decisions. Own the work from an ambiguous question through analysis to a clear recommendation and measurement of the result. Design and evaluate experiments, and advise Product, Marketing and Business Development. Make data quality, statistical limits and uncertainty explicit.

What you bring

  • 6+ years across product analytics, growth analytics, data science, analytics engineering or a closely related field.

  • Expert SQL and strong Python skills, including writing maintainable analytical code, debugging difficult queries and reviewing others’ work.

  • Experience building production data models and pipelines using dbt or an equivalent approach, with ownership of event schemas and trusted metrics.

  • Direct experience serving both Product and Product Marketing across D2C digital products and B2B or platform products, with experience in financial or other high-stakes transactional products in the U.S. market.

  • A record of measuring the customer journey from acquisition through retention, including segmentation, attribution, launch measurement, lifecycle analysis and growth experiments.

  • Strong statistical judgment across experimentation, causal analysis and small or biased samples. You can distinguish what the evidence supports from what remains uncertain.

  • Product and commercial judgment to challenge the question, choose the right measures and recommend action, backed by clear writing and independent ownership of the work.

  • Daily fluency with AI-assisted analysis and development tools that improve the speed and quality of your work.

STRONGLY PREFERRED

  • Direct experience with crypto, digital assets or onchain data.

  • Experience combining marketing, product, customer and onchain data.

  • Experience with lending, investing, marketplaces or financial infrastructure.

  • Experience as the first product analytics hire in a lean product organization.

Working at Kamino

You will work closely with the Staff Product Manager and Head of Product Marketing. Engineering and Design will be daily partners. You will also work directly with the CEO and CTO on company-level product and growth questions.

As Kamino's product portfolio grows, you will help define how the function should scale. The role stays close to the work, from instrumentation and data modeling through analysis and product recommendations.

This is a full-time, remote role open to candidates worldwide.

Compensation and benefits

The expected annual base salary range for this role is USD $160,000–$190,000. Kamino expects to offer a competitive package consisting of base salary, a performance-based bonus and long-term KMNO participation.

Final terms will reflect the candidate’s relevant experience, skills and agreed scope of the role.

Benefits and applicable employment terms will be documented as part of the formal offer.
